title: Add quantization profile types + JSON schema validation scaffolding
author: Benji Okafor
body: Summary: Introduces the core Quantization Profile data model (types + manifest) and a first-pass JSON Schema validation layer, plus internal config parsing scaffolding needed by the runtime/control-plane to safely consume Redwood-published profiles. This is the foundational plumbing for the upcoming opt-in Quantization Profile Library (route-scoped enablement and runtime resolution will follow in separate PRs). Motivation/Context: We need a versioned, hardware-scoped, runtime-compatible artifact format with strict server-side and client-side validation to prevent mis-scoped profiles from being published/activated. This PR focuses on (1) canonical types used across control-plane and runtime config loading, (2) JSON Schema for the profile manifest and constraints, (3) a small validation package + error semantics that downstream services can rely on. Details: Adds QuantizationProfileManifest (id, semver, model_ref, quant_method, dtype, calibration metadata), HardwareScope (vendor, sku, compute_capability, driver/runtime minimums), KernelConstraints (supported kernel families, max_seq_len bins, kv-cache compatibility flags), and ArtifactLayout pointers (relative paths + sha256 placeholders). Adds JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) + generated go bindings tests that ensure schema and structs don’t drift. Adds ValidateQuantProfileManifest() returning typed validation errors with stable codes (INVALID_SCHEMA, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, INVALID_HARDWARE_SCOPE, INVALID_KERNEL_CONSTRAINTS). Adds internal config scaffolding to parse a future RouteQuantizationPolicy block behind feature flag 'quant_profiles_library_v1' (parsing only; no behavior change). Out of scope: publishing APIs, signature verification, runtime resolution, and route enablement evaluation. Testing: unit tests for schema validation (good/bad fixtures), semver parsing, and error code mapping; CI runs schema conformance check. Rollout: no runtime behavior change; types/validator are unused by production request path until follow-up PRs wire them in. Checklist: [x] Schema + fixtures added [x] Backward/forward compatibility notes in code comments [x] Validation errors are non-leaky and safe for logs [x] Feature-flagged config parsing to avoid accidental activation.
commits: config: add parsing scaffolding for route quantization policy (flagged)
docs(internal): add notes on schema evolution + validation guarantees
review_conversation: 2024-11-07 Arjun Desai: The manifest looks good. Can we make calibration metadata explicit about dataset/promptset provenance so we can tie this to eval-harness runs later? Also suggest reserving a field for quality gates (pass/fail + link).

2024-11-07 Benji Okafor: Agree. I added calibration.promptset_id + calibration.source and left a placeholder calibration.eval_run_ref (string) with a comment that it will point to eval-harness run ids once wired.

2024-11-08 Quentin Harris: Please align naming with model-registry conventions: use model_ref (registry URI) instead of model_id, and make artifact layout relative paths only (no absolute URLs). Also ensure schema forbids unknown top-level keys; we’ve been burned by silent typos.

2024-11-08 Benji Okafor: Updated to model_ref and artifact_layout.{manifest_path,weights_path,calibration_path} as relative. Schema now sets additionalProperties=false at the top level and for nested objects where practical.

2024-11-09 Mateo Alvarez: On kernel constraints: can we avoid encoding runtime-specific kernel names? Maybe use a small enum of kernel families and keep the mapping internal. Also, do we want max_seq_len as bins rather than a single scalar?

2024-11-09 Benji Okafor: Switched to kernel_family enum (ex: TRTLLM, CUTLASS, XFORMERS_COMPAT) and changed seq len constraints to sequence_length_bins with min/max pairs. Mapping to real kernel impls stays internal.

2024-11-10 Marcus Lin: Two asks: (1) validation errors should not include user-provided JSON blobs in logs; (2) add a simple sanitization helper and tests so downstream services don’t accidentally log full manifests (which may include internal artifact paths).
2024-11-10 Benji Okafor: Added internal/logging/sanitize.go and updated validation errors to include paths + codes only (no raw JSON). Added sanitize tests and updated call sites to use it.

2024-11-11 Priya Natarajan: Config parsing scaffolding is fine but please ensure it’s fully gated. I don’t want any accidental enablement if someone adds the block in config. Also add a clear comment that this PR does not change routing behavior.

2024-11-11 Benji Okafor: Done. Parsing is behind quant_profiles_library_v1; without the flag we ignore the block and emit a single info-level message. Also added an explicit comment in pkg/config/route_quantization_policy.go and in the PR summary.
2024-11-12 Mateo Alvarez: Approved once you fix the gofmt issue in pkg/quantization/profiles/constraints.go.
2024-11-12 Benji Okafor: Fixed and pushed. Re-ran CI.
release_notes: Internal-only: Adds quantization profile manifest/types and JSON schema validation scaffolding; no production behavior changes.
